newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAFRICA UNION GROUP TO MEET MBOWENI ON LABOUR BILL.
newsitem.headline: SAFRICA UNION GROUP TO MEET MBOWENI ON LABOUR BILL.

text.p: South Africa's second largest trade union federation, the Federation of Unions of South Africa (Fedusa), said on Tuesday it would meet Labour Minister Tito Mboweni this week to discuss controversial proposed new labour laws.
"Fedusa will meet Labour Minister Tito Mboweni on Friday as part of his efforts to solve the crisis around the Basic Conditions of Employment Bill," a federation statement said.

Last week Mboweni met business and the leadership of the country's largest trade union federation, the 1.9-million member Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu), in an effort to reach agreement on controversial areas of the employment bill.
He said the talks had been "extremely difficult" but was optimistic that accommodation could be reached by September 15 when the bill was due to go to parliament.

The 500,000-strong Fedusa, which was formed earlier this year and includes technicians, administrative workers, nurses, doctors and teachers, said it had not participated in strikes around the bill, as it favoured negotiations.
The bill has been the subject of ongoing clashes between labour and business, with Cosatu staging a one-day national strike on June 2 to press business to revise its position.

Cosatu has threatened fresh national strikes in August to reinforce demands for a 40-hour working week to be phased in over not more than five years, six months' maternity leave of which at least four are paid and double payment for Sunday work.
Business is worried about the bill's wide scope and provisions which could raise employment costs to the point of creating obstacles to new jobs.
It has also suggested that the bill be linked to the government's planned presidential jobs summit in October.
